t: In a direct democracy the citizens vote on laws and policies themselves, in an open assembly or a referendum, rather than leaving them to elected representatives.
Athens from 508 to 322 BCE is the classic case: an assembly of male citizens, a council and juries chosen by lot governed, while women, slaves and resident foreigners had no vote.
Switzerland keeps the tradition alive in two cantonal open-air assemblies and in frequent national referendums and initiatives, devices also used by many US states.
dyk: At the open-air Landsgemeinde of Appenzell Innerrhoden men traditionally carry a sword as proof of their right to vote; women were admitted only after the Federal Supreme Court ruled in 1990 that the canton must let them vote.
ev: Cleisthenes reorganises the Athenians into ten tribes and creates the Council of Five Hundred
Ephialtes strips the Council of the Areopagus of most of its powers; pay for jurors follows under Pericles
The Athenians restore their democracy after the rule of the Thirty Tyrants
After the Lamian War, Macedon imposes a property qualification and ends the Athenian democracy
Switzerland’s federal constitution makes every constitutional amendment subject to a popular vote
Swiss citizens gain the popular initiative to propose amendments to the federal constitution
South Dakota becomes the first US state to adopt the initiative and the referendum
The Federal Supreme Court orders Appenzell Innerrhoden to admit women to its Landsgemeinde

f.power: The citizens themselves, meeting in an assembly or voting in referendums and initiatives; councils and officials prepare and carry out their decisions
f.legitimacy: Popular sovereignty: laws bind because the citizens who must obey them have voted on them, each with an equal vote
f.chosen: Officials are drawn by lot or elected for short terms and answer to the assembly or the voters, who may audit, recall or exile them
f.examples: Athenian democracy (508–322 BCE), the Landsgemeinden of the Swiss rural cantons (since the late Middle Ages), the New England town meetings (since the 1630s), the referendums and initiatives of the Swiss Confederation (since 1848), the ballot initiatives of California (since 1911)
